18. Dispute resolution

Informal negotiations

You and Footprint agree to attempt informal resolution of disputes, controversies, or claims relating to these terms for at least 30 days before arbitration, except for the exclusions below. Negotiations begin when one party gives written notice to the other.

Binding arbitration

If informal negotiations do not resolve a dispute, it will be resolved exclusively through binding arbitration unless expressly excluded. This provision replaces the right to sue in court and have a jury trial.

Arbitration is conducted under the American Arbitration Association's Commercial Arbitration Rules and, where appropriate, its Supplementary Procedures for Consumer Related Disputes ("AAA Consumer Rules"), available through the American Arbitration Association. Applicable consumer rules govern fees and arbitrator compensation. If the arbitrator finds those costs excessive, we will pay arbitration fees and expenses.

Proceedings may occur in person, through documents, by telephone, or online. The arbitrator issues a written decision; reasons need not be supplied unless a party requests them. Applicable law must be followed, and an award may be challenged if it is not. Unless applicable law or AAA rules require otherwise, arbitration occurs in New York, United States. A court may compel arbitration, stay proceedings, or confirm, modify, vacate, or enter judgment on an award.

Disputes proceeding in court must be brought in state or federal courts in New York, United States. The parties consent to their jurisdiction and waive personal-jurisdiction and inconvenient-forum defenses. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods and the Uniform Computer Information Transaction Act are excluded.

If an arbitration provision is illegal or unenforceable, disputes within that portion will be decided by a competent court in the jurisdiction specified above, and the parties consent to that court's personal jurisdiction.

Restrictions

Arbitration concerns only disputes between the individual parties. To the extent permitted by law, arbitration cannot be joined with other proceedings, conducted on a class-action basis, or brought in a representative capacity for the public or others.

Exceptions

Informal negotiation and arbitration requirements do not apply to disputes protecting, enforcing, or concerning the validity of intellectual property; allegations of theft, piracy, invasion of privacy, or unauthorized use; or claims for injunctive relief. If any part of this exception provision is unenforceable, the affected dispute will be decided by a competent court in the stated jurisdiction.
